records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: a new message
decisions.reason: The book's usual heading for a message from the LORD (see 3:16). Chapter 6 is addressed to the mountains of Israel, and chapter 7 to the land; both announce the judgment the signs of chapters 4-5 acted out.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. What follows is the LORD's oracle, which takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.heading: Against the mountains of Israel

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל־הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהִנָּבֵ֖א אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Son of man, set your face toward [the] mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,
pieces: Son of man, turn to face the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

L.2: Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel; prophesy against them,

R.2: Son of man, turn toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

decisions.choice: set your face toward: turn toward, with fixed purpose and hostility
decisions.reason: To set one's face toward a place is to turn to it with one's whole attention and a settled purpose. When the LORD tells Ezekiel to set his face toward a place or people, it is always to speak judgment against them (13:17; 21:2, 7; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2; 35:2; 38:2), and the LORD himself sets his face against those he judges (14:8; 15:7; Leviticus 20:3). Ezekiel may have turned bodily toward the land, far to the west of Babylon, as he spoke. Luke 9:51 uses the same picture of Jesus, who "set his face to go to Jerusalem". Later uses refer back to this note.

decisions.choice: the mountains of Israel: the hill country of the land
decisions.reason: Most of the land of Israel is hill country, and its hills and mountains were where the local shrines stood (verse 3; Hosea 4:13). Ezekiel speaks to the mountains as if they were people; the phrase "the mountains of Israel" is his own, and in 36:1-15 the same mountains are promised new life.

decisions.choice: set your face toward (L); turn to face (B); turn toward (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this phrase in Ezekiel. Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced and Readable give its sense, and "prophesy against" carries the hostility (m1). The sentence runs on into verse 3 at Literal.

records.source: וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְ֠הוִה לֶהָרִ֨ים וְלַגְּבָע֜וֹת לָאֲפִיקִ֣ים וְלַגֵּאָי֗וֹת הִנְנִ֨י אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֤יא עֲלֵיכֶם֙ חֶ֔רֶב וְאִבַּדְתִּ֖י בָּמֽוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and you will say, Mountains of Israel, hear [the] word of [the] Lord Yahweh! Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to the mountains and to the hills, to the ravines and to the valleys: See, I, I am bringing upon you a sword, and I will destroy your high places.
pieces: Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: I myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will wipe out your high places.

L.3: and say, Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to the mountains and the hills, to the gorges and the valleys: See, I, even I, am bringing a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.

R.3: Say to them: Mountains of Israel, listen to what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} has to say! This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says to the mountains, the hills, the ravines and the valleys: I myself am going to bring war on you. I will destroy your hilltop shrines.

decisions.choice: your high places: the local shrines
decisions.reason: The high places were shrines on hilltops and other raised sites, with altars and often a sacred pole or stone. Some were used for the LORD, many for other gods; the Law required worship at the one place the LORD would choose (Deuteronomy 12:2-5), and Josiah had torn them down (2 Kings 23:8-20), but they came back.

decisions.choice: I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places: Leviticus 26:30
decisions.reason: Leviticus 26:30 warns, "I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars, and cast your corpses on the corpses of your idols". Verses 3-6 follow it closely, with the same words for high places, incense altars and corpses.

decisions.choice: and to the valleys: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written consonants of "valleys" differ in spelling from the form the scribes' marginal note gives; the meaning is the same. The four kinds of landscape name the whole land, high and low, where the shrines stood.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD / The Lord GOD says this / This is what the Lord GOD says
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. The message Ezekiel is to deliver takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel. "High places" is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "hilltop shrines", as in the published histories. Readable says "war" for the sword, as in the Jeremiah wording for the sword with famine and plague.

records.source: וְנָשַׁ֨מּוּ֙ מִזְבְּח֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם וְנִשְׁבְּר֖וּ חַמָּֽנֵיכֶ֑ם וְהִפַּלְתִּי֙ חַלְלֵיכֶ֔ם לִפְנֵ֖י גִּלּוּלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And will be desolated your altars, and will be broken your incense altars, and I will make fall your slain before your idols.
pieces: Your altars will be laid waste and your incense altars smashed, and I will make your slain fall in front of your idols.

L.4: And your altars will be made desolate, and your incense altars will be broken, and I will make your slain fall before your filthy idols.

R.4: Your altars will be ruined and your incense altars smashed. I will kill your people in front of your idols.

decisions.choice: filthy idols: a word of contempt for idols
alternatives: idols, blocks of wood or stone
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's most frequent word for idols, used about forty times in the book and seldom elsewhere. Its origin is uncertain. It seems to be formed from the word for dung (the word of 4:12), perhaps given the vowels of the word for "detestable thing", so that it means something like "dung-gods"; others derive it from a word for blocks or logs. Either way it is a word of contempt, not a neutral name. Later uses refer back to this note.

decisions.choice: incense altars: small altars or stands
decisions.reason: The word occurs in Leviticus 26:30 and a few other places. It is usually taken as a small altar for burning incense; some think of a pillar connected with the worship of the sun. Small stone incense altars have been found at many sites in Israel.

decisions.choice: your slain before your idols: the gods they trusted cannot save them
decisions.reason: The worshipers will fall dead in front of the idols they served, and the idols will do nothing. Verse 13 returns to the picture.

decisions.choice: filthy idols (L); idols (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *gillulim* in Ezekiel. Literal keeps the contempt of the word (m1); Balanced and Readable say "idols", and the footnote gives the sense. Readable says "kill your people" for "make your slain fall".

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֗י אֶת־פִּגְרֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֑ם וְזֵרִיתִי֙ אֶת־עַצְמ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם סְבִיב֖וֹת מִזְבְּחוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will put the corpses of [the] sons of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.
pieces: I will lay the corpses of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in front of their idols and scatter your bones around your altars.

L.5: And I will lay the corpses of the sons of Israel before their filthy idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

R.5: I will put the dead bodies of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in front of their idols. I will scatter your bones all around your altars.

decisions.choice: your bones around your altars: the altars are defiled
decisions.reason: Human bones made a place unclean. Josiah defiled the altar at Bethel by burning on it bones taken from the tombs (2 Kings 23:14-16, 20). The shrines the people loved will be made unclean with their own bones.

decisions.choice: the Israelites / the sons of Israel (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As at 2:3. *Gillulim* is "filthy idols" / "idols" / "idols" (verse 4).

records.source: בְּכֹל֙ מוֹשְׁב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם הֶעָרִ֣ים תֶּחֱרַ֔בְנָה וְהַבָּמ֖וֹת תִּישָׁ֑מְנָה לְמַעַן֩ יֶחֶרְב֨וּ וְיֶאְשְׁמ֜וּ מִזְבְּחֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְנִשְׁבְּר֤וּ וְנִשְׁבְּתוּ֙ גִּלּ֣וּלֵיכֶ֔ם וְנִגְדְּעוּ֙ חַמָּ֣נֵיכֶ֔ם וְנִמְח֖וּ מַעֲשֵׂיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: In all your dwelling places the cities will be laid waste, and the high places will be desolate, so that will be laid waste and will be held guilty your altars, and will be broken and will cease your idols, and will be cut down your incense altars, and will be wiped out your works.
pieces: Wherever you live, the towns will be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars will be ruined and held guilty, your idols smashed and gone, your incense altars cut down, and what you have made wiped out.

L.6: In all your dwelling places, the cities will become wastes, and the high places will be made desolate, so that your altars will be laid waste and bear their guilt, and your filthy idols will be broken and come to an end, and your incense altars will be cut down, and your works will be wiped out.

R.6: In all the places where you live, the towns will be destroyed and the hilltop shrines ruined. Your altars will be ruined and condemned. Your idols will be smashed and gone. Your incense altars will be cut down, and everything you have made will be wiped out.

decisions.choice: bear their guilt: the altars are condemned
decisions.reason: As written, the verb means to be guilty or to bear guilt: the altars share the guilt of what was done on them. Read with a slight change of vowels, as some do, it means "be desolate", which matches the verb before it. The written form is followed.

decisions.choice: your works: the idols and objects of worship they made
decisions.reason: "The work of your hands" is the prophets' phrase for idols, which people make and then bow down to (Isaiah 2:8; Hosea 14:4).

decisions.choice: held guilty (B); condemned (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the written verb (m1). *Bamot* is "high places" (L, B) and "hilltop shrines" (R), as in verse 3.

records.source: וְנָפַ֥ל חָלָ֖ל בְּתֽוֹכְכֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will fall [the] slain in your midst, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: The slain will fall among you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.7: And the slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.7: People will be killed all around you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: and you will know that I am the LORD: the purpose of what the LORD does
decisions.reason: This is Ezekiel's refrain. In its several forms ("you will know", "they will know", "the nations will know") it occurs more than seventy times in the book. It names the purpose of both judgment and restoration: that Israel and the nations come to know, by what they see happen, that the LORD is who he says he is. To know here is to recognize and acknowledge, not only to be told. The words come from the account of the exodus, where the LORD acts so that Egypt and Israel "will know that I am the LORD" (Exodus 6:7; 7:5; 14:4, 18). What the exodus showed by rescue, the judgment will now show by destruction; and in chapters 36-39 the same words return for restoration (36:11; 37:6, 13). Later uses refer back to this note.

decisions.choice: the slain will fall in your midst: the dead among the survivors
decisions.reason: The "you" here is plural: the people of the land. The slain fall among those who are left, and it is the survivors who will come to know (verses 8-10).

decisions.choice: and you will know that I [am] the LORD (L); Then you will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for the refrain in Ezekiel. Literal keeps "and" and brackets "am", which Hebrew leaves out; Balanced and Readable begin a new sentence with "Then". Where the Hebrew has "they will know" (verses 10, 14), the same wording is used with "they".

records.source: וְהוֹתַרְתִּ֗י בִּהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֛ם פְּלִ֥יטֵי חֶ֖רֶב בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בְּהִזָּרֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And I will leave over, in that there will be to you escapees of [the] sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the lands.
pieces: Yet I will spare some of you. Some will escape the sword and live among the nations when you are scattered through the countries.

L.8: But I will leave a remnant, in that you will have some who escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the lands.

R.8: But I will let some of you live. Some of you will escape death in war and live among the nations, when you are scattered to other countries.

decisions.choice: I will leave a remnant: some will survive
decisions.reason: Even in the judgment, the LORD keeps some alive, as the few hairs were kept in the hem of Ezekiel's robe (5:3). The survivors are not spared because they were better (14:22-23), but so that they may remember and turn (verse 9).

decisions.choice: spare some of you (B); let some of you live (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means "leave over". Balanced and Readable say what it means for the people. Readable says "death in war" for "the sword".

records.source: וְזָכְר֨וּ פְלִֽיטֵיכֶ֜ם אוֹתִ֗י בַּגּוֹיִם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבּוּ־שָׁם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֜רְתִּי אֶת־לִבָּ֣ם הַזּוֹנֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־סָר֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י וְאֵת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם הַזֹּנ֕וֹת אַחֲרֵ֖י גִּלּֽוּלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָקֹ֨טּוּ֙ בִּפְנֵיהֶ֔ם אֶל־הָֽרָעוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֔וּ לְכֹ֖ל תּוֹעֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And will remember your escapees me among the nations where they have been taken captive there, how I was broken by their heart, the prostituting, which turned aside from me, and by their eyes, the prostituting [ones] after their idols; and they will loathe their faces for the evils which they have done, for all their abominations.
pieces: Then your survivors will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the nations where they have been taken captive. They will remember how I was broken by their hearts, which prostituted themselves and turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and by their eyes, which prostituted themselves by going after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evil they have done, for all their detestable practices.

L.9: And your survivors will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} among the nations where they have been taken captive, how I was broken by their heart that prostitutes itself, which turned aside from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and by their eyes that prostitute themselves after their filthy idols; and they will loathe themselves for the evils that they have done, for all their abominations.

R.9: Then those who survive will remember {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the nations where they have been taken as prisoners. They will remember how they broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart. Their hearts were unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and their eyes went after their idols like a woman with many lovers. They will hate themselves for the evil things they have done, for all the disgusting things they did.

decisions.choice: I was broken by their heart: the LORD grieved
alternatives: when I have broken their unfaithful heart
decisions.reason: The verb, as written, is "I was broken": the LORD speaks of himself as broken-hearted by his people's unfaithfulness, as a husband is by an unfaithful wife. It is a bold picture of God's grief. With a small change, some read "when I have broken their heart", that is, humbled them; the text as written is followed.

decisions.choice: prostitute oneself: unfaithfulness to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for prostitution. The prophets use it for Israel's going after other gods, as a wife who leaves her husband for lovers (Hosea 1:2; 4:12; Jeremiah 3:1). Ezekiel develops the picture at length in chapters 16 and 23.

decisions.choice: they will loathe their faces: they will loathe themselves
decisions.reason: "Their faces" stands for themselves. Remembering the LORD will bring the survivors to disgust at what they have done, the first step of turning back (20:43; 36:31).

decisions.choice: prostitute oneself (L, B); be unfaithful, like a woman with many lovers (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for *zanah* in Ezekiel, as in Judges 2:17 and Jeremiah 3:1. Readable says "they broke my heart" for "I was broken by their heart" (m1), and "hate themselves" for the idiom in m3. *To'evah* follows 5:9.

records.source: וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֤א אֶל־חִנָּם֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לָהֶ֖ם הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃פ
records.gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh; not in vain did I speak to do to them the evil this.
pieces: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and that I did not threaten in vain to bring this disaster on them.

L.10: And they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; not in vain did I speak of doing this evil to them.

R.10: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will know that I meant it when I said I would bring this disaster on them.

decisions.choice: this evil: this disaster
decisions.reason: The word means harm or calamity as well as moral evil. Here it is the disaster the LORD brings as punishment, as in Isaiah 45:7 and Jeremiah 18:8.

decisions.choice: they will know ... not in vain did I speak: the word proves true
decisions.reason: The refrain of verse 7, in the form "they will know". When the disaster comes, the survivors will know that the LORD's warnings were not empty words.

decisions.choice: and they will know that I [am] the LORD (L); Then they will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain as set at verse 7, with "they". Literal keeps "evil"; Balanced and Readable say "disaster" (m1).

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה הַכֵּ֨ה בְכַפְּךָ֜ וּרְקַ֤ע בְּרַגְלְךָ֙ וֶֽאֱמָר־אָ֔ח אֶ֛ל כָּל־תּוֹעֲב֥וֹת רָע֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֗ר בַּחֶ֛רֶב בָּרָעָ֥ב וּבַדֶּ֖בֶר יִפֹּֽלוּ׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Strike with your palm and stamp with your foot and say, Alas! because of all [the] abominations of [the] evils of [the] house of Israel, who by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence will fall.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Clap your hands, stamp your foot and cry, "Alas!" over all the evil and detestable practices of the house of Israel, for they will fall by sword, famine and plague.

L.11: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Strike with your palm and stamp with your foot and say, "Alas!" over all the abominations of evil of the house of Israel, who will fall by the sword, by famine and by pestilence.

R.11: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Clap your hands and stamp your feet, and cry out, "How terrible!" because of all the evil and disgusting things the people of Israel have done. They will die in war, from famine and from disease.

decisions.choice: strike with your palm and stamp with your foot: gestures that go with the message
decisions.reason: Clapping the hands and stamping the feet were strong gestures. In 25:6 the Ammonites clap and stamp in malicious glee over Israel's fall; here, with the cry "Alas!", they are more likely gestures of grief and alarm, though some take them as scorn. Ezekiel claps his hands again in 21:19, 22.

decisions.choice: Alas!: a cry of grief
decisions.reason: The word is a short cry, usually of grief or dismay. Ezekiel is to lament over the people even as he announces their fall.

decisions.choice: by the sword, by famine and by pestilence: the three judgments
decisions.reason: The three judgments of 5:12, as in Leviticus 26:25-26 and Jeremiah. Verse 12 says who will fall by each.

decisions.choice: Alas! (L, B); How terrible! (R); sword, famine and pestilence / plague / war, famine and disease
decisions.reason: "Alas!" is the cry Ezekiel says aloud, so it takes double quotation marks inside the oracle. Readable says "How terrible!", as for the cry of woe in Isaiah. The three judgments follow the Jeremiah wording. *To'evah* follows 5:9.

records.heading: Clap your hands and cry, Alas

records.source: הָרָח֞וֹק בַּדֶּ֣בֶר יָמ֗וּת וְהַקָּרוֹב֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפּ֔וֹל וְהַנִּשְׁאָר֙ וְהַנָּצ֔וּר בָּרָעָ֖ב יָמ֑וּת וְכִלֵּיתִ֥י חֲמָתִ֖י בָּֽם׃
records.gloss: The far [one] by the pestilence will die, and the near [one] by the sword will fall, and the [one] remaining and the [one] preserved by the famine will die; and I will complete my wrath on them.
pieces: Those far away will die of plague, those nearby will fall by the sword, and whoever is left and has been spared will die of famine. So I will spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them.

L.12: The one far off will die by pestilence, and the one near will fall by the sword, and the one who remains and is spared will die by famine; and I will spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on them.

R.12: People who are far away will die of disease. People who are nearby will be killed in battle. Anyone who is still alive will die of hunger. That is how I will pour out all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on them.

decisions.choice: far, near, remaining and spared: no one will escape
alternatives: the one who remains and is besieged
decisions.reason: Far and near together mean everyone. The last word can mean "spared" or "besieged" (the same verb is used of a city under siege, Isaiah 1:8): those who survive the plague and the sword, or those shut in the city, will die of famine.

decisions.choice: pestilence, sword, famine / plague, sword, famine / disease, battle, hunger
decisions.reason: The three judgments as in 5:12. The Hebrew uses singular forms for each group; Literal keeps "the one" and Balanced and Readable say "those" and "people". *Chemah* is "wrath" at Literal and Balanced and "anger" at Readable.

records.source: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בִּֽהְי֣וֹת חַלְלֵיהֶ֗ם בְּתוֹךְ֙ גִּלּ֣וּלֵיהֶ֔ם סְבִיב֖וֹת מִזְבְּחֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם אֶל֩ כָּל־גִּבְעָ֨ה רָמָ֜ה בְּכֹ֣ל׀רָאשֵׁ֣י הֶהָרִ֗ים וְתַ֨חַת כָּל־עֵ֤ץ רַֽעֲנָן֙ וְתַ֨חַת֙ כָּל־אֵלָ֣ה עֲבֻתָּ֔ה מְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָֽתְנוּ־שָׁם֙ רֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ לְכֹ֖ל גִּלּוּלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you will know that I [am] Yahweh, when are their slain among their idols around their altars, on every hill high, on all [the] tops of the mountains, and under every tree luxuriant, and under every terebinth leafy, the place where they gave there a smell of soothing to all their idols.
pieces: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, as their slain are lying among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill and on all the mountaintops, under every spreading tree and every leafy oak, the places where they offered pleasing aromas to all their idols.

L.13: And you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when their slain are among their filthy idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the heads of the mountains, and under every luxuriant tree, and under every leafy terebinth, the place where they offered a soothing aroma to all their filthy idols.

R.13: Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Their dead bodies will lie among their idols around their altars. They will lie on every high hill and on every mountaintop, under every green tree and every leafy oak. Those are the places where they offered sweet-smelling sacrifices to all their idols.

decisions.choice: on every high hill ... under every luxuriant tree: the places of pagan worship
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 12:2, which tells Israel to destroy the places where the nations served their gods "on the high mountains and on the hills and under every luxuriant tree". It is used for the shrines of Israel and Judah in 1 Kings 14:23, 2 Kings 17:10 and Jeremiah 2:20; 3:6.

decisions.choice: a soothing aroma: the smell of sacrifice that pleases
decisions.reason: This is the Law's phrase for an offering the LORD accepts (Genesis 8:21; Leviticus 1:9). The people gave to their idols what belonged to the LORD alone (16:19; 20:28).

decisions.choice: terebinth: a large tree, often oak or terebinth
decisions.reason: The word names a large shade tree, the terebinth or the oak; the two are not always kept apart in Hebrew. Such trees were often sites of worship (Hosea 4:13).

decisions.choice: spreading tree, leafy oak (B); green tree, leafy oak (R)
decisions.reason: The refrain as set at verse 7, with "you". Literal keeps "luxuriant" and "terebinth"; Balanced and Readable use more familiar words. Readable splits the long sentence and says "sweet-smelling sacrifices" for "a soothing aroma".

records.source: וְנָטִ֤יתִי אֶת־יָדִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת־הָאָ֜רֶץ שְׁמָמָ֤ה וּמְשַׁמָּה֙ מִמִּדְבַּ֣ר דִּבְלָ֔תָה בְּכֹ֖ל מוֹשְׁבֽוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And I will stretch out my hand against them, and make the land a desolation and a waste, from [the] wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against them and make the land a desolate waste from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: And I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against them and make the land a desolation and a waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, in all their dwelling places; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.14: I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against them. I will make the land empty and ruined everywhere they live, from the desert to Diblah. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: from the wilderness to Diblah: the whole land
alternatives: more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblah
decisions.reason: No place called Diblah is known. The Hebrew letters for d and r look alike, and many read Riblah, a town in Syria on the northern edge of the land (Numbers 34:11; 2 Kings 25:6). "From the wilderness" in the south "to Riblah" in the north would mean the whole land. The words can also be read "more desolate than the wilderness of Diblah". The name is kept as written.

decisions.choice: I will stretch out my hand: the LORD acts in power
decisions.reason: The stretched-out hand is the LORD's power at work, in judgment as against Egypt (Exodus 7:5) and in Ezekiel against Israel and the nations (14:9, 13; 25:7).

decisions.choice: and they will know that I [am] the LORD (L); Then they will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain as set at verse 7. Readable says "use my power" for "stretch out my hand" (m2).
